newsitem.title: POLAND: British Sugar to increase investment in Poland.
newsitem.headline: British Sugar to increase investment in Poland.

text.p: British Sugar Plc has offered to expand its investment in Poland by buying a 38-percent stake in the large Robczyce sugar refinery in the south-east, PAP news agency said on Thursday.

PAP quoted British Sugar's regional director Andrew Armstrong as saying his company, present in Poland since 1989 and with stakes in three refineries, was interested in taking up to 25 percent of Poland's sugar processing capacity.

"Our ambition is to develop the sugar industry in Poland, especially in the southeastern part of the country," PAP quoted Armstrong as saying after a meeting with Robczyce's management and authorities of Rzeszow province in which the plant stands.

Poland expects to produce a record 2.2-2.25 million tonnes of white sugar in the 1996/97 season against 1.58 million in 1995/96, the head of the Sugar Council grouping sugar refineries said last month.
PAP reported that investors from Germany, Canada and Poland were also bidding for a stake in Robczyce in a tender likely to be concluded in March.
